extract:
Holly Humberstone is an English singer-songwriter from Grantham, Lincolnshire, who emerged in the late 2010s as one of the most distinctive new voices in British alternative pop. Raised in a rambling, slightly dilapidated house with three sisters, she has often cited the rural, isolated quality of her upbringing as central to the introspective, diaristic character of her songwriting. She began writing and uploading music while still a teenager, and by the turn of the decade had been picked up by Polydor Records' Darkroom imprint in the UK, aligning her with a wave of confessional British pop contemporaries including Phoebe Bridgers' broader sphere of influence and peers like Sigrid and Maisie Peters.

Her breakthrough came with the 2020 single Falling Asleep at the Wheel, a fragile, synth-tinged ballad that became the title track of her debut EP later that year. The EP introduced the production partnership that would define much of her early catalogue: her work with producer Rob Milton (formerly of Dog Is Dead), whose lo-fi, textural approach complemented her cracked, intimate vocals and piano-led writing. Songs like Overkill, Drop Dead and Deep End established her template of dryly observed heartbreak and family vignettes set against muted electronic arrangements. The recognition was swift: she was longlisted for the BBC Sound of 2021 poll and won the Rising Star award at the 2022 BRIT Awards.

A second EP, The Walls Are Way Too Thin, arrived in late 2021, sharpening her songwriting on tracks like Scarlet, a sinewy, frustrated meditation on a friend's relationship that became one of her most beloved songs. Around this period she was hand-picked by Olivia Rodrigo to open the UK and European dates of the Sour Tour, dramatically expanding her audience, and she also toured with Lewis Capaldi. A collaboration with The 1975's Matty Healy and George Daniel produced the standalone single Please Don't Leave Just Yet in 2021, cementing her connections to the broader Dirty Hit and Polydor-adjacent British indie-pop ecosystem.

Her debut album Paint My Bedroom Black followed in October 2023, expanding her sonic palette with contributions from Daniel and Healy alongside Milton. Tracks like Antichrist, Into Your Room and the title song pushed her further toward atmospheric, slightly abrasive textures while retaining the conversational lyricism that drew listeners in the first place. Critics broadly welcomed the record as a confident step up from the EPs, even if some felt it lacked a single defining moment to match Scarlet. The album consolidated her standing as a thoughtful, literate songwriter rather than a chart-chasing pop act, and she continued to tour it extensively through 2024, including supporting Girl in Red and headlining her own dates across the UK, Europe and North America.

Humberstone remains an active and rising figure in British alternative pop, working primarily within the orbit of Darkroom and Polydor while maintaining the homespun, songwriter-first identity that distinguished her early work. Her legacy at this still-early stage is as one of the key British artists who helped define a strain of millennial and Gen Z confessional pop in the early 2020s, bridging the bedroom-pop intimacy of the streaming era with a more traditional singer-songwriter craft.
title: Holly Humberstone
